scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 4 · KP04 Decomposing the test error

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Off the training set, prediction and noise are independent, so test error splits in two

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: left shows where the prediction and the noise each come from; right is a three-step proof, the cross term vanishes at step ②.

scene-u01-pnew1-9.name: text#9
scene-u01-pnew1-9.text: Fixes every parameter of the model

scene-u01-pnew1-12.name: text#12
scene-u01-pnew1-12.text: A function of the training data

scene-u01-pnew1-23.name: text#23
scene-u01-pnew1-23.text: This is exactly why KP01 keeps test and training sets disjoint

scene-u01-pnew1-24.name: text#24
scene-u01-pnew1-24.text: What we want is how far $\hat f$ is from $f$, but $f$ is hidden;

scene-u01-pnew1-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew1-25.text: what we can compute is how far $\hat f$ is from $y$

scene-u01-pnew1-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew1-26.text: The gap depends on whether prediction and observation "collude"

scene-u01-pnew1-31.name: text#31
scene-u01-pnew1-31.text: ② Cross term: independence plus zero-mean noise

scene-u01-pnew1-34.name: text#34
scene-u01-pnew1-34.text: ③ The third term is KP03's $\mathbb{E}(\varepsilon_0^2)=\sigma^2$

scene-u01-pnew1-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew1-36.text: Computable error is distance from truth plus the noise floor

scene-u01-pnew1-37.name: text#37
scene-u01-pnew1-37.text: The cross term vanishes thanks to independence and zero-mean noise

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 4 · KP04 Decomposing the test error

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Check by hand: with noise only $\pm1$, mean squared error $1.25=0.25+1$; the cross term averages to $0$

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: on the line, teal is the truth, purple the prediction, blue the two possible observations; below, each case is computed, then averaged. [Added example]

scene-u01-pnew2-38.name: text#38
scene-u01-pnew2-38.text: Each case half the time: average

scene-u01-pnew2-44.name: text#44
scene-u01-pnew2-44.text: In a single case the cross term isn't $0$ ($\pm1$); averaging removes it

scene-u01-pnew2-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew2-45.text: So the identity holds in expectation: $\mathbb{E}\big((\hat f_0-y_0)^2\big)=(\hat f_0-f_0)^2+\sigma^2$ (with $\hat f_0$ fixed)

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 4 · KP04 Decomposing the test error

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Summed over the test set: empirical error minus the noise floor is the true error

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: formula on top; the bar uses the source's example ($n_{te}=50$, $\sigma^2=4$, $\mathbf{err}=300$) to split 300 in two.

scene-u01-pnew3-13.name: text#13
scene-u01-pnew3-13.text: Whole bar: empirical error $\mathbf{err}=300$ (computed on the test set)

scene-u01-pnew3-19.name: text#19
scene-u01-pnew3-19.text: No model can shake it off

scene-u01-pnew3-22.name: text#22
scene-u01-pnew3-22.text: Per point: divide both sides by $n_{te}$

scene-u01-pnew3-24.name: text#24
scene-u01-pnew3-24.text: $\approx$: equal in expectation; closer with more test points

scene-u01-pnew3-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew3-28.text: Reading $\mathbf{err}$ alone makes the model look much worse

scene-u01-pnew4-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew4-3.text: Week 4 · KP04 Decomposing the test error

scene-u01-pnew4-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew4-5.text: Seeing the identity in a simulation: in 300 repeats the computable error equals "true error $+\ \sigma^2$"

scene-u01-pnew4-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew4-6.text: How to read: each dot is one run (draw 15 points, fit a line, score on 20000 new points); dots on the dashed $y=x$ line mean the identity holds.

scene-u01-pnew4-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew4-8.text: $f(x)=1+2x-1.5x^2$, $\sigma=0.3$, fitted with a line (a biased model)

scene-u01-pnew4-331.name: text#331
scene-u01-pnew4-331.text: Dots spread along the diagonal but stay on it

scene-u01-pnew4-332.name: text#332
scene-u01-pnew4-332.text: (all 300 dots drawn; lecture's program, fixed seed)

scene-u01-pnew4-336.name: text#336
scene-u01-pnew4-336.text: Computable error is true error plus noise floor

scene-u01-pnew4-337.name: text#337
scene-u01-pnew4-337.text: Largest gap in a single run: $0.0077$

scene-u01-pnew4-344.name: text#344
scene-u01-pnew4-344.text: The model need not be right

scene-u01-pnew4-345.name: text#345
scene-u01-pnew4-345.text: The truth is a parabola, the model a line (biased);

scene-u01-pnew4-346.name: text#346
scene-u01-pnew4-346.text: the identity still holds: it only needs independent test points

scene-u01-pnew4-348.name: text#348
scene-u01-pnew4-348.text: Source: idl-2026-fall lectures/lec04-kp04-test-error-decomposition.md §3, caption mc (simulation added in the lecture)

scene-u01-pnew5-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew5-3.text: Week 4 · KP04 Decomposing the test error

scene-u01-pnew5-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew5-5.text: The noise floor is the same for every model: subtracting it keeps the ranking, if test points stay unused

scene-u01-pnew5-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew5-6.text: How to read: left, two models' bars share the same floor (schematic); right, what happens when the condition breaks.

scene-u01-pnew5-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew5-8.text: Two models on one test set (schematic, not measured)

scene-u01-pnew5-21.name: text#21
scene-u01-pnew5-21.text: Lowest $\mathbf{err}$ is the same model as lowest $\mathbf{Err}$

scene-u01-pnew5-22.name: text#22
scene-u01-pnew5-22.text: Why test error can measure generalization

scene-u01-pnew5-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew5-25.text: Condition broken: test points were used

scene-u01-pnew5-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew5-26.text: Leaked into training or used to tune (KP01's two cheats)

scene-u01-pnew5-29.name: text#29
scene-u01-pnew5-29.text: The cross term is no longer $0$

scene-u01-pnew5-31.name: text#31
scene-u01-pnew5-31.text: $\mathbf{err}$ too small: the model looks better than it is

scene-u01-pnew5-35.name: text#35
scene-u01-pnew5-35.text: ✗ Lower empirical error always means lower true error (needs independence)

scene-u01-pnew5-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew5-36.text: ✗ $\sigma^2$ can be ignored ($\mathbf{err}$ always has extra $n_{te}\sigma^2$)

scene-u01-pnew5-37.name: text#37
scene-u01-pnew5-37.text: ✗ The identity applies to the training set (Figure 6)

scene-u01-pnew6-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew6-3.text: Week 4 · KP04 Decomposing the test error

scene-u01-pnew6-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew6-5.text: Training points flatter: the tighter the fit, the further training error drops below new-data error

scene-u01-pnew6-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew6-6.text: How to read: left, four points and two models; right compares their three errors (same scale). [Added example]

scene-u01-pnew6-39.name: text#39
scene-u01-pnew6-39.text: Blue dots $y=(2.5,\,2.5,\,4.5,\,4.5)$; rose ticks show noise

scene-u01-pnew6-40.name: text#40
scene-u01-pnew6-40.text: Memorizer: $\hat f_i=y_i$, right on every training point

scene-u01-pnew6-65.name: text#65
scene-u01-pnew6-65.text: ① Both models' training error is below their new-data error

scene-u01-pnew6-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew6-66.text: ② The memorizer: training error $0$, yet worst on new data ($2$ vs $1.2$)

scene-u01-pnew6-67.text: ③ Don't compare models or estimate true error with training error
